title: Access, Tiered Participation and Links
summary: How FMIs set fair and open access criteria, the risks hidden in tiered participation and client clearing, and the exposures created by links between infrastructures.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How FMIs set fair and open access criteria, the risks hidden in tiered participation and client clearing, and the exposures created by links between infrastructures.
Learning Objectives: Evaluate participation requirements for fairness, risk basis and openness
Identify risks from indirect participants and client clearing
Assess the risks of links and interoperability arrangements
Syllabus: Risk-based access criteria and suspension or exit of participants
Tiered participation: concentration on large direct participants
CCP links, CSD links and interoperability exposures
Intended Audience: Supervisors and overseers of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs, payment systems and trade repositories in securities authorities and central banks
Financial stability, risk modelling and operational resilience specialists who assess FMI risk
Resolution, policy and international staff working on FMI recovery, resolution and cooperative oversight
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of capital markets, payments or financial stability work is helpful. Familiarity with the PFMI is useful but not required.
Core Reading: CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
CPMI-IOSCO, Application of the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures to Stablecoin Arrangements (2022)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Tokenisation (2024)
